title: Status page brief with operator checklist and customer verification phrases
content:
Purpose and audience:

This is a working draft for concise status page updates, operator step checklist, and a short customer-facing verification kit that Product/CS/Support can reuse when an inference degradation affects tenant responses (partial correctness, delayed streaming, or truncated structured output). Audience: customer-success, support L2/L3, incident commander, and account teams preparing outbound comms.

Top-line summary (for status page):
- Short headline: "Intermittent inference responses affecting subset of tenants — mitigation in progress"
- One-line detail: "We observed sporadic degraded outputs and elevated latency for some requests routed to the US-west inference fleet. Full routing fallback and integrity checks are underway; customer-facing verification options below."

Operator checklist (immediate steps for status page cadence):
1) Confirm scope: ticket INF-4237 — quantify impacted tenants by tenant-id and region (SLO/usage buckets).
2) Lock a single source-of-truth doc — add incident timeline entries to this doc (owner: Marisol Chen).
3) Draft first statuspage entry (short, plain language) and publish as "investigating" + update Slack #customer-ops.
4) Enable safe fallback routing rule (if policy exists) to route affected customers to fallback model variant or region. Note: coordinate with routing-engineering (oncall).
5) Trigger limited replay/consistency checks on a representative sample (10 tenants) and collect evidence (request ids + timestamps).
6) If replay shows acceptable integrity, prepare customer replay offer language (below).
7) For enterprise customers with strict SLAs, notify account team with specific impact metrics and recommended actions within 30 minutes of detection.
8) Publish follow-up: partial mitigation or full mitigation with verification link and next steps.
9) After restore: prepare customer-facing postmortem summary and suggested remediation steps.

Customer verification kit (self-serve, short instructions to include in status updates):
- Why we ask for request ids: these allow us to trace the exact server-side trace and confirm whether the output was affected by KV-cache inconsistency, routing, or model fallback.
- How customers can verify:
  * If you have request ids: send three examples (1 high-priority, 2 typical) and we will run integrity checks and provide a redline diff for text outputs or cosine-similarity for embeddings.
  * If no request ids: run a quick test prompt (we suggest a short seed prompt specific to your workload) and paste the response id; we will cross-check latency and tokenization metadata.
  * For streaming issues: run a 30-token streaming test and capture timings (client timestamps vs server timestamp returned in headers).
- What we return: a per-request verification summary (status: OK / Modified / Truncated), attached diffs, and recommended replay or replay-decline choices.

Customer choiceboard (short choices to present in communications):
- Option A: "Auto-replay" — we replay affected requests on your behalf to the last known-good model variant (subject to consent).
- Option B: "Evidence-only" — we provide verification artifacts (diffs, traces) and you decide whether to replay or ignore.
- Option C: "No action" — you receive a final postmortem; no replays are performed.
- Option D: "Prefer fallback" — permanently route your tenant to a pre-approved fallback variant until further notice.

Sample status page messages (3-tier progression) — keep wording short and consistent:
1) Investigating (first 10–20 minutes):
   - Title: "Investigating degraded inference responses — US-west"
   - Body: "We are investigating reports of intermittent degraded outputs and elevated latency for some requests in US-west. Impacted tenants may see unusual responses or delayed streaming. Engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes."
2) Mitigation in progress (next update):
   - Title: "Partial mitigation applied — routing fallback enabled for affected tenants"
   - Body: "We have applied a routing fallback for affected tenants and are validating outputs. Some customers may still experience transient errors while verification completes. If you want us to replay affected requests, see the verification choices in our status details or contact support."
3) Resolved + verification (closure):
   - Title: "Service restored — integrity checks underway"
   - Body: "Service has been restored and routing has returned to normal. We are completing integrity checks and will publish a post-incident summary with recommended actions and replay options. If you observed incorrect outputs and want replays, follow the verification kit steps or open a ticket with request ids."

Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise template) — one paragraph + bullets:
- One-paragraph summary (customer language): "On 2026-10-29 between 08:12–09:44 UTC a subset of inference requests routed through our US-west serving fleet returned intermittent degraded or truncated outputs. Root cause: a race during cache population after an autoscaling event which could result in incomplete KV state for some worker shards. Impact: approximately 0.8% of tokens served to 42 tenants experienced partial truncation or minor content skew.
- Immediate mitigations taken: we enabled conservative routing to last-known-good model variants, refreshed shard state, and rolled out a hotfix to the cache-population path.
- What we will do to prevent recurrence: robust guardrails on shard warmup, additional debug tracing gated behind a short-term feature flag, and a new canary for autoscale events.
- Customer options and next steps: If you were impacted and want a replay, provide request ids (examples attached) or opt-in to our auto-replay. For enterprise support, contact your account manager for prioritization and evidence packages."

Evidence and verification examples (what we'll send back):
- Per-request status: OK / Modified / Truncated
- Short diffs (line-based) for text generative outputs
- Cosine-similarity and fingerprint for embedding outputs (we will provide vector similarity and top-k nearest neighbor differences)
- Streaming latency timeline: client timestamp vs server event stamps

Sample account email snippet (concise):
Hi <Account Owner>,
We detected intermittent degraded outputs for your tenant on 2026-10-29. We have mitigated and restored service. If you want us to replay affected requests, reply to this email with up to three request ids and we will prioritize verification and replay. Attached: short verification checklist and timeline.

Regulatory / legal phrasing (short options):
- Minimal/regulatory-friendly: "No customer data was exfiltrated. We worked under account-level isolation; evidence packages are available on request."
- Expanded: "We’ve preserved request logs and cryptographic evidence for audit. We can produce a signed evidence bundle for enterprise customers on request (legal review required)."

Things to watch / unresolved items (notes to operator):
- Confirm final impacted tenant list and token counts by 2026-11-03 EOD.
- Validate hotfix in Canary for 72 hours, then schedule a post-deploy audit.
- Open follow-up engineering ticket to add durability check on shard warmup: GH #987 (linked above).
- Decide replay automation policy for small customers vs enterprise customers (policy draft needed).

Snippets for status page UI fields (short, copy-paste friendly):
- Short title (max 64 chars): "Intermittent degraded inference — US-west (mitigation applied)"
- Impacted features: "text generation, streaming, embeddings (subset)"
- Public update line: "We applied a routing fallback and are validating integrity; customers may request replays via support."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Legal: do we need a signed evidence bundle template? (ask legal by EOD 2026-11-03)
- Billing: do we offer replay-cost credits automatically or by request? propose options to finance.
- Communications: get approval for final customer postmortem language by product and engineering leads.

Quick links:
- Incident ticket (internal): JIRA-INF-4237
- Runtime hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- Canary dashboard: https://internal.redwood.com/canary/us-west
- Slack thread: #customer-ops (pinned message with timeline)

Notes to self (drafty):
- Keep phrasing plain-language, avoid deep technical jargon on public status page.
- Keep a separate, more detailed technical postmortem for internal distribution (include logs and traces).
- For large customers, prepare a short meeting/call with engineering to walk through evidence and replay process.

End of draft.

(Use this as the single-source-of-truth for customer-facing comms for INF-4237 until final postmortem is signed off.)
